bib.title: Why do LLMs attend to the first token?

question: Why do LLMs learn to put heavy attention on the first token (attention sinks) and how does the model use it?
hypothesis: Sinks let deep, long-context Transformers avoid over-mixing, so sinks should be stronger in larger models and with longer training context, and should form at the first token whether or not it is bos.
contributions: Argue sinks control over-mixing, linking rank collapse, representational collapse and over-squashing, with Gemma 7B measurements (Sec 3).
Show bigger models and longer training contexts have stronger sinks, in Llama 3.1 and own pre-training runs (Sec 4).
Show sinks form regardless of how bos is included in pre-training, but fixing bos changes how the sink is built (Sec 5).

method.summary: Theory (multi-head over-squashing bound, rank vs representational collapse) plus measurements: perturbation tests and head inspection on Gemma 7B, sink-rate on Llama 3.1 8B/70B/405B, and ~120M-parameter models trained from scratch varying context length and packing/masking/bos strategy.
method.task: Mechanistic analysis of attention sinks; next-token pretraining of small LMs for ablations

120M model trained with causal masking and bos only as document boundary (no fixed bos) forms a sink at the first token whether or not bos is given at inference.

results.claim: Sink strength grows with pre-training context length; nearly absent at context 128.
results.setup: ~120M LLaMA2-style models, contexts 128 to 2048, equal tokens per step, 5B tokens total, ~20000 steps; values read only from Fig 5 (no numbers in text)
results.note: Appendix A.2 says 'training loss curves' for Fig 7, but panel (b) is loss and the caption calls them validation-style curves; main text calls them validation loss curves.
results.quote: essentially no sink formation at a context length of 128 and much stronger formation for the longer contexts

results.claim: Mean attention weight on first token rises under bos: in a typical prompt in Llama 405B almost 80% of attention goes to bos.
results.setup: Llama 3.1 405B, typical prompt; details only said to be in Section 4.2 which gives no separate figure
results.quote: almost 80% of the attention is concentrated on the ⟨bos⟩token

results.claim: Theorem 3.2 bounds token-to-token sensitivity by C_max^L times a sum over causal paths of head-summed attention coefficients, so mass on a low-value sink limits the spread of perturbations.
results.setup: Proof assumes queries/keys independent of values and does not differentiate through softmax; submultiplicative induced norms

results.claim: Rank collapse (distance to mean < Delta/2) implies representational collapse (< Delta); converse not true.
Perturbing one token ('greatest' to 'best') spreads much more through Gemma 7B layers when bos is removed.
results.setup: Gemma 7B, one Shakespeare paragraph, token count held constant; qualitative heatmap, Fig 2
results.note: No numeric summary; colour bar to ~1600

results.claim: A first-layer Gemma 7B head attends to bos by default and fires on apostrophe; the bos value norm is smallest, giving an approximate no-op.
results.setup: Gemma 7B, one head, one 23-token example, Fig 4

limits: Bounds assume queries and keys independent of values and skip the softmax derivative.
Gemma 7B benchmark drops (Table 3) conflate sinks with a missing, out-of-distribution bos; the paper's own Table 2 shows models without a fixed bos do not need bos.
Hardware/optimizer/lr/seeds of the 120M runs deferred to Gu et al.; no repeats or error bars.
Authors suspect longer training would sharpen sinks; 5B tokens only.
Footnote: mechanisms eventually disperse at longer context per Velickovic et al. 2024.
Evidence is correlational: shown consistent with over-mixing, not shown causal.
Appendix B text refers to Figure 4 where Figure 9 is meant.
